items.body:
Lilith is the untamed part. She marks what they were shamed out of, and what comes back stronger once they stop apologizing for it. Evergreen's Lilith is in Capricorn, meaning they refuse and reclaim seriously, patiently, and with a plan, and what they want most is achievement and structure. Their untamed side is ambition without the apology: wanting the position, the money, the authority. Someone taught them that hunger is ugly. It is fuel for the climb. Pushed too far, this side of them can tip into rage saved up until it picks its own moment. At their best, they turn the banned feeling into honest power, and their refusal makes room for other people to be real too.

It's in their 10th house, meaning this side of them is on public display: career, reputation, and what they're known for. It is visible at the top: the ambition or the scandal they fear being known for. A reputation built on the real version holds better.

The Midheaven sits at the very top of their chart. It shows how they go after their career and their bigger purpose, and how the world sees them at their most visible. Here they are judged by what they do, not by who they are underneath. Evergreen's Midheaven is in Pisces. Their calling runs through imagination and compassion: creating, healing, or helping in ways that do not fit a tidy job title. Meaning matters more to them than status, every time. Paired with one solid structure, the vision stops being a dream and becomes a body of work.

They swing between pushing too hard and giving up halfway, and other people's authority rubs them the wrong way. Underneath is a harsh inner critic that questions every move before it is made. Physical effort and long projects suit that drive, because their will gets stronger with age and ends up carrying them further than talent. That's Evergreen's Mars square Saturn: drive and structure pulling against each other until the friction builds muscle.

Four of their planets square off in a closed ring: two oppositions crossing each other, pressure on every corner. Nothing in this pattern rests, and no single planet carries it alone, so life keeps presenting the same four-sided problem from rotating angles. The reward for that relentlessness is real: people with a Grand Cross can carry loads that would flatten everyone else, once they stop trying to fix all four corners at the same time.

It runs as a cardinal pattern: it acts first and asks later.

With Taurus on their 1st house, identity, the body, and self-presentation take shape slowly and become more reliable over time. Rushing usually creates more work than it saves. Venus rules Taurus, so the real activity for this house runs through their Venus in Cancer, in their 2nd house of money, belongings, and self-worth. They value what has history and care in it, and they bond through feeding, hosting, and remembering. What they love, they keep; the risk is keeping it past its season. Because of this, their identity may become clearer through the way they handle money, worth, and values. Timing: They may notice more activity here when a transit reaches their Venus or when a current planet moves through their 1st house.
The 9th house is belief, travel, higher learning, and the long search for what life means.
